name: TI 74181

extra_images.caption: The synthesized gate-level netlist, drawn by Yosys from our own RTL.

description: 16 logic and 16 arithmetic functions on one chip. Our dry run: rebuilt from the datasheet, every input combination checked.

name: Intel 4004
description: The first commercial single-chip microprocessor: 46 instructions, 4 bits wide. Rebuilt with its ROM and RAM companions, and tested against the Busicom calculator firmware.

name: Intel 8080
description: The 8-bit processor that went into some of the first personal computers: 244 instructions, 64 KB of memory. Rebuilt from Intel's manual and checked with the full 8080 instruction exerciser.

name: MOS 6502
description: The cheap 8-bit processor of the Apple II and the Atari 2600: 151 official instructions. Rebuilt from MOS's manuals and checked with the standard functional test and a decimal-mode test.

name: Zilog Z80
description: The 8-bit CPU of the ZX Spectrum, the Amstrad CPC and the Sega Master System: the 8080 plus a second register set, IX/IY, block moves and bit instructions. Rebuilt from the manuals and checked with the zexdoc instruction exerciser. Our own sky130 layout is on the card; it does not yet meet hold timing.
